subject: business-studies
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A multinational company (MNC) is a business that:
options: Trades only in its home town
Operates and produces in more than one country
questions.explain: A multinational operates in several countries, often producing and selling across national borders.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a stakeholder in a business?
questions.explain: Stakeholders are any groups with an interest in the business, including employees, customers and suppliers.

questions.q: If the exchange rate of the pound rises (strong pound), UK exports tend to become:
questions.explain: A stronger pound makes UK exports more expensive for overseas buyers, which can reduce export demand.

questions.q: During a recession (a downturn in the business cycle), businesses often experience:
questions.explain: In a recession consumer spending falls, so many businesses see lower demand and sales.

questions.q: In a partnership, profits are usually:
questions.explain: Partners typically share the profits (and losses) of the business according to their agreement.

questions.q: What does 'limited liability' mean for the owners of a private limited company (Ltd)?
options: The business has limited time to operate
Owners can lose only the amount they invested
Owners are personally responsible for all business debts
questions.explain: Limited liability means shareholders can only lose the money they invested, not their personal assets.

questions.q: What is enterprise in a business context?
options: The skill of spotting an opportunity and taking the risk to act on it
questions.explain: Enterprise involves identifying a business opportunity and taking the risk of acting on it.

questions.q: Consumer protection law mainly exists to:
options: Set the prices of all goods
Ensure goods are safe, as described and of satisfactory quality
questions.explain: Consumer law protects buyers by requiring goods to be safe, as described and of satisfactory quality.

questions.q: Why might rapid growth be a risk for a business?
options: Growth removes the need for planning
Growth always lowers costs with no downside
It can stretch cash flow and management, causing problems if not controlled
questions.explain: Growing too quickly can overstretch cash and management, so growth carries risk as well as reward.

questions.q: One advantage of globalisation for a UK consumer is:
options: A wider choice of products, often at lower prices
questions.explain: Globalisation gives consumers a wider choice of goods from around the world, often at competitive prices.

questions.q: A drawback of a business relying heavily on new technology is that:
options: It can be costly to install and staff may need retraining
questions.explain: New technology often involves high set-up costs and staff retraining, even though it can improve efficiency.

questions.q: The 'boom' stage of the business cycle is usually marked by:
options: High consumer spending, rising demand and growing output
Falling demand and many business closures
questions.explain: In a boom, the economy grows strongly with high spending, rising demand and increasing output.

questions.q: What is the main role of an entrepreneur when starting a business?
options: To work only as an employee for a larger firm
To guarantee the business will make a profit
To take a risk by organising resources to set up a business
questions.explain: An entrepreneur takes the risk of combining resources (land, labour, capital) to create a new business.

questions.q: A key benefit of buying a franchise rather than starting from scratch is that:
options: There is no risk of failure at all
The franchisee keeps all profit and pays nothing to the franchisor
The franchisee can ignore the franchisor's rules
The business uses an established brand and proven business model
questions.explain: A franchisee trades under an established brand with a proven format, reducing some of the risk of a start-up.

questions.q: Which of the following are the three factors of production?
questions.explain: The factors of production are land, labour and capital (with enterprise often added as a fourth).

questions.q: What is 'organic growth'?
options: Growth from within, such as by selling more products or opening new branches
Growth by merging with another firm
Growth by taking over a competitor
questions.explain: Organic (internal) growth comes from expanding the existing business rather than merging or taking over another.

questions.q: Stakeholders such as the local community might pressure a business to:
options: Reduce noise and pollution from its operations
questions.explain: Local communities are stakeholders who may pressure a business to limit pollution, noise and other local harms.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the 'dynamic nature' of business?
options: Profit always stays the same each year
Businesses never change once set up
All businesses must be public limited companies
Markets and conditions constantly change, so businesses must adapt to survive
questions.explain: The dynamic nature of business means conditions change constantly, so firms must adapt to survive and grow.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a business plan?
options: To replace the need for any finance
To guarantee the business will succeed
To set out the aims, strategy and finances of the business to guide it and attract investment
questions.explain: A business plan outlines aims, strategy and financial forecasts, helping to guide decisions and secure funding.

questions.q: Globalisation has made it easier for businesses to:
options: Trade and operate across international borders
questions.explain: Globalisation has increased trade and the ability of firms to operate across countries.

questions.q: High inflation can be a problem for businesses because:
options: Rising costs may squeeze profit margins and customers may buy less
questions.explain: High inflation raises the cost of materials and wages and can reduce real incomes, hurting profits and demand.

questions.q: If interest rates fall, the most likely effect is that:
options: Borrowing and consumer spending tend to increase
questions.explain: Lower interest rates make borrowing cheaper, which tends to encourage borrowing, investment and consumer spending.
